title: Lantern and Orchard
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of the Orchard Uprising, census taker Aurelio Vance arrives at the print shop of master typeface cutter Henrik Eriksen to count heads—and instead uncovers a hidden archive: proof that the Eriksen family forged the land grants the ruling Consulate now uses to dispossess the orchard districts. Falling for the cutter's watchful daughter Paloma, Aurelio must choose between his oath to the state and getting the true record into print before the victors' historians burn every press that might contradict them. As the city rises and the print shop becomes a target, Paloma cuts the evidence into type with her own hands while Aurelio smuggles it past the censors; they succeed at terrible cost—Henrik dies defending the formes, the uprising wins only a partial victory, but the printed truth survives in a thousand pamphlets, and Paloma and Aurelio, changed and grieving, carry the lantern of honest record into whatever comes next.
about_author: Emrys Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed newspapers in coastal municipal collections. Lantern and Orchard is their second novel, drawn from a lifelong fascination with the people who kept ink flowing when it was dangerous to do so.

chapters.title: The Counting Man
chapters.summary: Aurelio Vance, POV. A weary census taker works his route through the orchard district, tallying households he is forbidden to look at too closely. He notices the print shop's shutters, its silence, the daughter who never meets his eye. Beat: quiet unease beneath bureaucratic routine.

chapters.title: Low Profile, Busy Hands
chapters.summary: Paloma Eriksen, POV. Inside the shop, Paloma grinds punches and sorts type while her father Henrik burns papers after dark. She has learned invisibility as a craft. The chapter establishes the family's careful choreography of secrecy. Beat: tension coiled inside domestic routine.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. Returning to correct an arithmetic error, Aurelio asks about a fourth family member the ledger doesn't explain. Henrik's answer is smooth; Paloma's hands go still over the type case. Aurelio leaves unconvinced—and unable to stop thinking about what he saw. Beat: the crack opens.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Cleaning her father's locked cabinet, Paloma finds a punch-cut seal matching the Consulate's crest—an heirloom that should not exist. Henrik catches her and, for the first time, tells her a fragment of the truth: their name was not always Eriksen. Beat: inheritance revealed as burden.

chapters.title: The Orchard Districts
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. Filing his census returns, Aurelio notices the district maps have been redrawn to erase old orchard boundaries—the same boundaries hinted at in the Eriksens' documents. His supervisor warns him off curiosity. Beat: duty begins to chafe.

chapters.title: Bread and Banned Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. At market, Paloma witnesses soldiers seize a pamphleteer's press. She slips home shaken, and she and Aurelio—waiting in line, pretending coincidence—exchange first real words. Beat: fear sharpened into attraction.

chapters.title: The Cabinet Opens
chapters.summary: Henrik, POV. Henrik finally shows both young people the archive: forged land grants, original deeds proving the orchards belong to tenant families, and letters naming the Consulate's founders as thieves. He has waited thirty years for someone worth trusting. Beat: the secret becomes a shared weight.

chapters.title: Oath and Appetite
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. Torn between oath and conscience, Aurelio copies nothing—but memorizes everything. He attends a Consulate banquet where officials toast the 'orderly settlement' of the orchard question. Beat: complicity tasted and rejected.

chapters.title: Cutting the First Letter
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma begins secretly cutting new type from the archive's most damning page, working nights. Henrik resists—printing means death—but she argues that a record no one reads is just kindling. Beat: resolve hardening into action.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. The Consulate sends Victor Sarn, a court historian, to Vellamare to write the official account before the expected unrest. Sarn requisitions all commercial presses, including the Eriksens'. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Searches and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Soldiers search the shop; the archive hides behind a false wall of standing type. Aurelio, present in his official capacity, misdirects the sergeant—a small betrayal of his uniform that cannot be taken back. Beat: lines crossed, trust sealed.

chapters.title: Rumors of the Rising
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. The city simmers: dockworkers strike, orchard tenants refuse rents, and Sarn drafts a history that calls it all foreign agitation. Aurelio realizes the victors' version will be printed within weeks. Beat: urgency overtakes caution.

chapters.title: The Lantern in the Loft
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Working by lantern light in the type loft, Paloma and Aurelio set the first pages together, fingers touching over the composing stick. Henrik watches his daughter fall in love with a government man and says nothing. Beat: tenderness inside danger.

chapters.title: Sarn's Offer
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. Sarn, shrewd, offers Aurelio promotion and immunity if he reports any seditious printing. Aurelio accepts the meeting, refuses the bargain obliquely, and walks out knowing he is now suspected. Beat: the trap half-sprung.

chapters.title: Proof Sheet
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The first proof comes off the hand press: the true land grants, typeset and legible. Henrik weeps reading his grandfather's confession in ink. But the noise draws a neighbor's attention, and word begins to travel. Beat: triumph shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Presses
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. Sarn orders the seizure of every press in the district. Aurelio races ahead of the soldiers to warn the Eriksens, choosing his side irrevocably. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Formes in the Night
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. With soldiers at the docks, the family distributes the locked formes to trusted printers across the city—four shops, four chances. Paloma gives Aurelio the master copy to carry. Beat: scattering the seed.

chapters.title: Henrik's Stand
chapters.summary: Henrik, POV. Soldiers breach the shop; Henrik refuses to open the false wall and dies defending it, buying time as the last forme goes out the back. Paloma escapes through the type loft window. Beat: grief as climax's first blow.

chapters.title: The City Rises
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. The Orchard Uprising erupts; barricades rise as Aurelio runs the gauntlet with the master pages sewn into his coat. Sarn nearly catches him at the customs house. Beat: climax—flight, pursuit, near-loss.

chapters.title: Ink on Every Door
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Dawn after the fighting: the pamphlets appear nailed to doors across Vellamare, the true record in ten thousand copies. The uprising holds the district but not the capital; the Consulate retreats to negotiate. Beat: costly, partial victory.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historians
chapters.summary: Aurelio, POV. In the aftermath, Aurelio testifies before the new assembly, submitting his census notes alongside the printed grants. Sarn flees the city. Aurelio resigns his post, keeping only his pen. Beat: accountability, quiet and earned.

chapters.title: Lantern and Orchard
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Spring: Paloma reopens the shop under her own name, cutting a new typeface called Lantern. She and Aurelio plant an orchard behind the press room—for Henrik, for the record, for what survives. Beat: resolution rooted in grief, love, and continuity.
